subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group-chat isolation be solved with sender-scoped sessions and memory namespaces, automatic per-user group subagents, or a Feishu plugin experiment before adding any core or SDK contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior changes cross-user memory, skill/config authority, lifecycle cleanup, quotas, and message-routing boundaries that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design The Feishu Isolation Seam First
options.body: Use current sender/topic session and subagent binding primitives as inputs, define memory/config/lifecycle/security boundaries, and then implement the approved seam.

options.title: Prototype In The Feishu Plugin
options.body: Validate routing, cleanup, quotas, shared/private memory, and admin controls in the Feishu plugin before promoting any SDK or core contract.

options.title: Defer Heavy Group Subagents
options.body: Keep narrower session-routing, threading, and skill-preference issues open while avoiding automatic group subagent orchestration for now.

recommendation.title: Design The Feishu Isolation Seam First
recommendation.body: Use current sender/topic session and subagent binding primitives as inputs, define memory/config/lifecycle/security boundaries, and then implement the approved seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily Feishu channel behavior, and the plugin metadata identifies @m1heng as the community maintenance signal.
